article.headline: Ted Lasso season 4 episode 9 honors late actor Anthony Head with tribute card
article.summary: Apple TV's Ted Lasso included a tribute card for actor Anthony Head in Season 4, Episode 9 following his death in June 2026 at age 72.
article.body:
Ted Lasso paid respects to Anthony Head, who died in June 2026 at age 72 from complications due to pneumonia. The Apple TV comedy series featured a tribute card before the end credits of Season 4, Episode 9, titled "Mae Rides the Bus."

Head played Rupert Manion, the former owner of AFC Richmond and ex-husband of Rebecca Welton, across 18 episodes in the series' first three seasons. His family released a statement saying he "passed away peacefully of complications due to pneumonia, surrounded by his family." They added: "It has been, and forever will be, an honour and a privilege to be his daughters, and to have witnessed firsthand the impact both he and his work have had on so many."

Cast members shared their condolences publicly. Brett Goldstein called Head "a brilliant actor" and "the best person," describing him as "infinitely charming and kind and fun and a joy." Hannah Waddingham reflected on his influence on her performance: "There is no Rebecca without Rupert. He undoubtedly made my Rebecca what she was. He was one of the finest gentlemen I've ever met." Jeremy Swift posted: "Goodbye Tony, we adored you, Rest in Peace my friend." Actress Annette Badland remembered him as "funny, bright, inclusive, generous" with "wry humor" and "a very beautiful man."

article.headline: Two years removed from surgery, Musgrove returns to Padres' playoff roster vs. Cubs
article.summary: Joe Musgrove, the 33-year-old Padres right-hander who underwent Tommy John surgery in October 2024 and missed nearly two years from major-league action, was added to San Diego's Wild Card Series roster as a reliever.
article.body:
Musgrove last pitched in a major-league game on October 2, 2024, when he exited a Wild Card Series start against the Braves with the elbow injury that led to reconstructive surgery. Nearly two years later, he's back on a postseason roster, this time as a reliever after a recovery marked by multiple setbacks.

The 33-year-old San Diego native has shown encouraging signs in recent appearances. Across three August rehab starts at Triple-A, Musgrove averaged 94.4 mph with his fastball, up from 92.9 mph in 2024. He expressed optimism about his progress, saying "I do feel the most optimistic I've felt at any time in the last two years."

Musgrove's track record with the Padres suggests he remains a capable pitcher despite the extended layoff. In four seasons with San Diego, he posted a 123 ERA+, a 3.68 FIP, and a 4.18 K/BB ratio across 97 starts. He threw the first no-hitter in Padres history in 2021. Over his full MLB career, he has 26 relief appearances, giving him experience in that role.

The Padres added him to their 11-man pitching staff as they prepare to face the Cubs in the Wild Card Series. Game 1 is scheduled for Tuesday at 7 p.m.
